claims.text: The driver's own trace measures his qualifying in-geofence dwell at 200 seconds — a single run from 12:45:20 to 12:48:40 covering 21 fixes — which is well short of the 300-second free waiting period in force for this trip. POL-NS-01(c) is therefore broken: the fee is not chargeable even on the driver's own best case.

The waiting period in force is 300 seconds, not 180: trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec reads 300, and POL-NS-01(c) takes the free waiting period from platform_policy where the record carries it, as fee_schedule.resolution_rule directs ('platform_policy first, defaults otherwise'). The 180-second default in fee_schedule.defaults never comes into play on this record, so the driver needed 300 seconds of continuous in-geofence dwell and delivered 200.

Because the effective in-geofence dwell of 200 seconds falls 100 seconds short of the required 300, POL-NS-06 applies directly: the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, and no driver compensation is payable. The refund is the cancellation-fee line, which is the whole of the $4.00 charged.

POL-NS-06 limb (i) cannot rescue the driver's shortfall. Dwell may only be accumulated across separate in-geofence intervals, and this trace contains exactly one such interval (run_count 1), so there is no second interval to sum; and limb (i) independently requires a present and populated traffic_advisory of type KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT, whereas EV-ADVIS-00412-01 is MISSING. I disclose that artifact's impairment: it carries weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and its absence is itself citable but can exonerate nobody.

POL-NS-01(d) fails as well. The trip was terminated by the driver at 12:48:40, which is precisely the last fix of the 200-second qualifying run and therefore before the required 300-second dwell had elapsed; a termination that precedes the elapse of the required dwell cannot satisfy limb (d).

The rider was not the problem. The rider's own track carries 23 fixes across the entire 12:45:20 to 12:48:38 window, every one of them stationary (distinct speeds 0.0 km/h) and every one within 76 m of the pickup pin — comfortably inside the 100 m rider presence radius for a STANDARD zone. POL-NS-06 refunds the fee whether or not the rider was present, and on this record the rider was present and waiting at the pin.

The driver's statement that he 'messaged the rider, no reply' cannot save the fee: POL-NS-06 refunds a waiting-period shortfall whether or not the rider responded to messages. The chat log shows one driver message ('exit A') at 12:45:45 and nothing further, and trip_record.in_app_calls is empty — the driver terminated the trip at 12:48:40 without ever placing a call.

This case should be decided, not held. The two artifacts that carry the deciding facts — the trip record and the GPS trace — are both COMPLETE at weight 1.0; there is no admissible contradiction between them on arrival, dwell or rider presence; the rider and driver have no disputes between them in the trailing 90 days; rider no_show_disputes_30d stands at 1, below POL-NS-09(d)'s threshold of 3; and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip (1 no-show termination against 120 completed trips in 30 days, far short of both the count and the rate limb). No POL-NS-09 trigger is engaged.

The driver's appeal to 'this rider's history speaks for itself' is not a ground of decision. POL-GEN-01 makes prior_no_show_flags a lifetime counter and context only, and the only rider no-show field the policy reads is no_show_disputes_30d, which is 1. No adverse finding about this trip may be built from the rider's lifetime record, and the driver's own untarnished history cannot make out limb (c) of POL-NS-01 where his trace shows only 200 seconds of dwell.

The money block is clean, so the refund is the full figure charged. platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd is $4.00 and fare_breakdown.cancellation_fee is $4.00 — the net figure — so the ledger reconciles as POL-NS-08(d) requires and no fare defect impairs it; payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so the rider is still carrying the disputed $4.00 and the refund of that line is the whole of the remedy due.

claims.text: The driver arrived, and POL-NS-02 is satisfied on the trace itself: the export carries 50 fixes at 10 s cadence with 100% coverage and no gaps, of which 21 consecutive fixes fall inside the STANDARD arrival radius of 50 m at the pickup pin, running from 12:45:20 to 12:48:40, with a closest approach of 3.89 m. The rider's 'you never showed' reading of this trip is contradicted by the platform's own telemetry, and the arrival limb of the no-show test is not in issue.

The arrival marker is true and POL-NS-05 has no application: the trip record's 'arrived' event at 12:45:20 is the exact timestamp of the first qualifying in-geofence fix, and the derived arrival facts describe that interval as an interval in which the driver held position inside the 50 m radius. The marker was therefore not posted from beyond 300 m and not posted at 15 km/h or above, so this is not a false-arrival event, no clock recomputation beyond 12:45:20 arises, and the driver's waiting time runs exactly as the record states - and the case is not one where a false-arrival referral should be entered against him.

The rider was not at the pickup point the driver was sent to. The rider's own device (23 fixes, 12:45:20 to 12:48:38, no gaps, stationary at 0.0 km/h throughout) sits between 68.0 m and 76.0 m from the pickup pin for the whole waiting window, mean 72.2 m - outside the 50 m arrival radius - while the driver held position 3.89 m to 50 m from that same pin. The trip record accordingly shows no boarding event and a termination for RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three codes the clause recognises, so the reason code recorded is a truthful description of what happened: the rider did not appear where the booking placed her.

The rider cannot be exonerated under POL-NS-04, whose three limbs are conjunctive. Limb (a) fails on the face of the chat export: it contains exactly two messages, the system notice 'Your driver has arrived' at 12:45:21 and the driver's own locating message 'exit A' at 12:45:45 - neither of them sent by the rider. The rider sent no locating or coordinating message at all during the waiting window, so the clause fails at its first limb whatever the geometry shows under limb (c), and neither the 120-second reply clock of limb (b) nor the fault allocation of POL-NS-03 is reached.

Nothing on this record suggests the driver is a fee-farmer: the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check requires both 4 or more no-show terminations in 30 days and a ratio above 0.08 against completed trips, and the driver's figures are 1 and 1/120 = 0.008, so neither limb is met. But I do not found anything on the driver's rating, acceptance rate, lifetime trips or his 'never had a fee reversed' assertion: under POL-GEN-01 every one of those is context only and cannot carry a finding about this trip. The case turns on the timestamps alone.

I concede the point that decides the fee, rather than stretch the record. The driver's qualifying in-geofence dwell is 200 seconds (21 fixes, 12:45:20 to 12:48:40), against a free waiting period in force of 300 seconds for this trip (the record's own platform_policy.free_wait_sec, consistent with the 300-second minimum dwell for STANDARD) - a shortfall of 100 seconds. On those figures POL-NS-01 is not satisfied, because limb (c) requires a continuous dwell of at least the free waiting period and limb (d) requires the termination to fall at or after the moment that dwell elapsed, which 12:48:40 does not; POL-NS-06 therefore makes the $4.00 cancellation fee not chargeable and refundable to the rider in full, and POL-NS-07 cannot pay the driver compensation it conditions on POL-NS-01 being satisfied in full. The amount itself is not in issue - the $4.00 line reconciles with the fee in force for this trip - but the chargeability is, and on the arithmetic it fails.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties — this is the provisional ruling on trip TRP-00412. The driver's waiting time was too short, so the $4.00 no-show cancellation fee is refunded to the rider in full.

The figures. The driver accepted at 12:40:30, his first qualifying in-geofence fix at the Sembawang MRT (Exit A) pin is at 12:45:20, and the trip was terminated at 12:48:40. That is a single continuous stationary dwell inside the STANDARD 50 m arrival radius of 200 seconds (21 qualifying fixes, closest approach 3.89 m). The free waiting period in force on this trip is 300 seconds, read from trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec as fee_schedule.resolution_rule directs ('platform_policy first, defaults otherwise'); the 180-second fee_schedule default never comes into play on this record. The dwell is therefore 100 seconds short.

Why that decides it. POL-NS-01(c) requires a continuous dwell of at least the free waiting period in force before a RIDER_NO_SHOW fee is chargeable, and the same shortfall breaks limb (d): a termination at 12:48:40 precedes the elapse of the dwell the clause requires. POL-NS-06 then makes the cancellation fee not chargeable and refundable in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages. POL-NS-06 limb (i) cannot rescue the fee: the trace shows one in-geofence interval only (run_count 1), so there is no second interval for it to add to the first, and the traffic_advisory the limb requires, EV-ADVIS-00412-01, is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) — its absence is citable but exonerates nobody, and asserting it against a MISSING artifact is precisely what POL-NS-09 guards against.

Claims I accepted. The driver's own concession that the fee fails on the 200-second dwell is accepted and is the ground of this ruling, as is the rider's parallel arithmetic and her reading of the 300-second waiting period. The arrival itself is not in issue: POL-NS-02 is satisfied by 21 consecutive in-radius fixes, and POL-NS-05 does not fire, because the 'arrived' marker at 12:45:20 coincides exactly with the first qualifying in-geofence fix — it was neither posted from beyond 300 m nor posted at 15 km/h or more — so no false-arrival referral is entered against the driver. POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider and I do not rely on it: the chat log holds only the system arrival notice and the driver's 'exit A', and the rider sent no locating or coordinating message, so limb (a) fails at once, whatever limb (c) shows. That does not help the driver either, because POL-NS-06 refunds on the dwell arithmetic alone.

Claims I rejected or put aside. The driver's submission that the rider was not at the pickup point is rejected: the rider's track shows 23 stationary fixes 68.0 m to 76.0 m from the pin (mean 72.2 m) across the whole window, and the threshold that governs rider presence is the 100 m rider_presence_radius_m for a STANDARD zone, not the 50 m driver-arrival radius. In any event the rider's presence or absence cannot save a fee that fails on dwell. The driver's 'this rider's history speaks for itself' is put aside under POL-GEN-01: prior_no_show_flags (6) and rating (3.82) are context only and cannot carry any finding about this trip; the only rider no-show field the policy reads is no_show_disputes_30d, which is 1, and the driver's own rating (4.97) and lifetime trips (4,200) are equally context only. Nothing is discarded for this — both advocates cited those fields only to say they are context-only, which is correct, so no claim was discarded on that ground.

No escalation and no referral. No POL-NS-09 trigger is engaged: my confidence (0.95) is above the 0.70 floor; the trip record and the GPS trace agree on arrival, dwell and termination, so there is no unresolvable contradiction; neither party shows a dispute with the other in the trailing 90 days; rider no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the threshold of 3; the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip (1 no-show termination in 30 days against 120 completed trips, ratio 0.008, and both limbs must be met); and the deciding facts rest on COMPLETE, weight-1.0 artifacts, so no POL-NS-08(a)–(d) impairment makes escalation mandatory. No clause produces a referral on this disposition: POL-NS-05(ii) does not fire because the arrival marker is true, and POL-NS-01's driver-education item is for a mis-selected reason code, whereas RIDER_NO_SHOW is one of the three codes limb (d) recognises.

The money, and execution. fare_breakdown.cancellation_fee is $4.00, which reconciles with platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of $4.00, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect; payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so the rider is still carrying the disputed $4.00. The refund is the whole of that cancellation-fee line: $4.00. No driver compensation is payable: POL-NS-07 conditions the payout (80% of the $4.00 fee, the money block's $3.20) on POL-NS-01 being satisfied in full, and it is not. The monetary effect, $4.00, is below the $8.00 execution threshold, so this provisional ruling executes automatically; either party may appeal once, within 30 days, under POL-GEN-04.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the $4.00 no-show cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-00412 is not chargeable. I order it refunded in full to the rider. No driver compensation is payable and no referral is made.

Why the fee fails. POL-NS-01 makes a no-show fee chargeable only if all four of its conditions hold. The first two do: the trip record carries the driver's 'arrived' event at 12:45:20, and the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00412) places him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius at that exact moment, with 21 consecutive qualifying fixes and no gaps, so the marker is genuine — POL-NS-05 does not fire and no false-arrival entry is made against the driver. The measured hold therefore falls 100 seconds short. POL-NS-01 limb (c) fails, and limb (d) fails as well because the trip was terminated by the driver at 12:48:40, at the very last fix of that run and before the required 300-second dwell had elapsed.
